<!-- pr-reviewer: 38875bbcd896331ca86d6e87de2945ed352e25fe -->
**Needs changes before merge.** The cap change works: the 76-file corpus is unchanged and 10208.STEP imports again at the 60 M budget. The fallback has one real hole, though. A pass where two faces run out at once can keep a smeared mesh, and the range clause that keeps sc_logo out has no test.

### What looks good
- **Cap.** 150 M is a fixed constant with a pinned lower bound. The default-cap refusal test (120 s limit) also kills an over-large cap: a 1 G mutant fails it. Dropping budget scaling is the right call.
- **Disclosure.** The fallback reports the kept pass's own `kept.tol` (step_refine.rs:88-94). That value flows into `ReducedFidelity`, so the #864 laws tighten or refuse by name. A coarser mesh never reaches a verdict silently.
- **Soundness argument.** truck's `sub_parameter_division` (truck-geotrait 0.4.0, `algo/surface.rs`) tests one jittered interior point per cell against the bilinear patch. On a C0 surface over a compact box that deviation goes to 0, so the division ends. That holds for C0 kinks and cusps too: only position continuity matters for termination, and a fold is checked by the same midpoint test as any accepted pass. Trim loops that cross a knot don't matter, because the proof covers the whole knot range.
- **Wording.** The new refusal text no longer calls a continuous face "discontinuous". `step_guard` stays under 400 lines, and the tests moved out cleanly.

### Results (merged with upstream main 2d15a617, locally on macOS, debug unless noted)
The self-hosted runner check returned 403 (counted as none online), so everything ran locally.

| Suite | Result |
|---|---|
| app lib | 217 passed, 1 ignored |
| import_step_guard | 6 passed (19 s) |
| step_budget / step_chord_units / step_fidelity / step_nesting | 6 / 3 / 2 / 8 passed |
| model_fidelity / large_models / regression_models | 9 / 3 (+1 ignored) / 2 passed |
| import / mcp_model / bore_facet_sagitta / stock_export | 26 / 5 / 2 / 2 passed |
| camcraft-geometry (8 binaries) | 85 passed |
| `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets --no-deps -- -D warnings` | clean |

**Corpus (release, default budget).** 76 STEP files: 13 testdata files, 58 user models, h5, sc_logo, sc_logo_softjaws, End Caps and Colt. For each file I compared facet count, chord, and an order-independent hash of every coordinate's bits, this head against upstream main. **76/76 identical.** The only differences are the cap number in the two refusals: `bspline_discontinuous.step` (face #53) and `sc_logo.step` (face #836, still refused by name). I re-ran the first 36 files on current main and they matched the #1546 review's corpus bit for bit, so the rest were compared against that record. No file took the fallback.

**10208.STEP at the 60 M budget:** **imports, 14,866,333 facets, chord 5e-3, hash 4d71e3300a88fb51 in 159 s** - bit-identical to main before #1546 (same count, chord and hash; 173 s then). Current main refuses it on face #1073.

**Refusal time (release, quiet machine, two runs each):** `bspline_discontinuous.step` 7.0-7.1 s (main 1.2 s); `sc_logo.step` 10.5-10.6 s (main 1.75 s). These are the worst measured. The GUI runs `ImportModel::new` on a worker thread (`crates/ui/src/state.rs`, `import_rx`), so the UI does not freeze. The import is not cancellable mid-flight, but it is bounded. With several runaway faces in one pass, each spends its own 150 M; rayon runs them in parallel, so the wall time grows roughly with faces ÷ cores (note, not blocking).

### Requested before merge
1. **Two faces running out in one pass can keep a smear.** `Guarded::tripped()` (step_guard.rs:264-273) reports only the *first* tripped face: `self.meters.iter().position(|m| m.tripped())`. Suppose a lower-index proven-continuous face and a higher-index face that may jump both run out on the same refinement pass. The trip is then reported `continuous: true` and `refine` keeps the coarser mesh, which is exactly the #1536 smear on the second face. I confirmed it with a local unit test (not pushed) on the `bspline_discontinuous.step` shell. With meter 0 (a plane, proven) and meter 5 (the jump face) both past the cap, `tripped()` returns `Trip { index: 0, kind: "elementary surface", continuous: true }`. **Fix:** the pass is continuous only if *every* tripped face is proven and in range. For example, prefer the first tripped face that is not proven, then fall back to the first trip, so the refusal names the face that may jump. Pin it with a two-meter test like the one above.
2. **The range clause only covers the pass that tripped, not the pass whose mesh is kept.** `Meter::reset()` (step_guard.rs:85-88) clears `outside` at the start of every pass, and `tripped()` reads only the failing pass's flag. truck derives the division range from boundary points projected at that pass's tolerance, so the range can differ between passes. The kept, coarser pass may have divided over a wild range (the sc_logo #836 failure: a few huge cells over the trimmed region converge into a smear) while the finer pass stayed in range. **Fix:** make `outside` sticky across passes, or carry it with `Kept`. Once any pass of a face divided outside its range, a later trip on it is not proven.
3. **The range clause is not pinned at the composition level.** Mutation `tripped_ignores_range` (dropping `&& !m.outside` in `tripped()`) **survives** every suite: `a_division_outside_the_surface_range_is_flagged` only checks the flag, never that a trip with the flag set refuses. That clause is the only thing keeping sc_logo.step refused (your own finding). Please add a test where a `Guarded` trip with `outside` set reports `continuous: false`, so the clause cannot be dropped silently.

### Mutation check (each applied, lib `geometry::import` + `import_step_guard` run, reverted)
| Mutation | Result |
|---|---|
| cap 140 M | killed (headroom pin) |
| cap 141 M | survived (bound is 5 x 28.07 M = 140.35 M, as designed) |
| cap 1 G | killed (default-cap refusal hits its 120 s limit) |
| knot multiplicity `<= degree + 1` | killed |
| B-spline finite-point check dropped | killed |
| NURBS `w >= 0` | killed |
| NURBS x/y/z finiteness dropped | **survived** |
| NURBS `w.is_finite()` dropped | **survived** |
| non-finite knot check dropped | **survived** |
| `within` range check always true | killed |
| `within` finiteness dropped | **survived** |
| `reset()` keeps `outside` | killed (see item 2: this mutant is arguably the safer behaviour) |
| `tripped()` ignores `outside` | **survived** (item 3) |
| swept surface proven (`=> true`) | **survived** |
| elementary surface not proven | survived (harmless: elementary faces keep truck's own unmetered division, so they practically never trip) |
| fallback arm refuses | killed |

The `swept => true` survivor matters more than its size suggests. A swept surface built from a jumping B-spline curve would get the fallback, so please add a one-line test (an extruded curve is not proven). The finiteness survivors are cheap one-liners too (a NaN weight and a NaN knot in `step_continuity::tests`).

### Notes (not blocking)
- **Wrong remedy text after a cap fallback.** The reduced-fidelity refusals say "re-import with a larger STEP facet budget" (`model_fidelity.rs:58`, `:311`), and the log line at step.rs:314 says "bounded by memory or by the kernel's least tolerance". When the coarser mesh was kept because a face ran out of evaluations, a larger budget changes nothing, so the advice is misleading. A follow-up could carry the reason with `Kept` and say "a face needed more than N evaluations". No corpus file reaches this path today.
- **Near-zero positive weights.** A NURBS weight such as 1e-300 passes `w > 0`. The surface is continuous, so termination holds, but it is nearly a pole. The coarser mesh is checked at one point per cell and can miss a narrow spike, which is the very feature the finer pass was chasing. A relative weight floor (e.g. `w > 1e-9 * max w`) before calling a face proven would be more conservative.
- Closed/periodic surfaces: B-spline/NURBS faces are not periodic in truck. Periodic elementary surfaces keep their own division, so I see no issue there.
- Process: conventional subject, `Changelog:` line, `Fixes #1568`, decision file present, no CHANGELOG.md/snapshot/process files touched, provenance line on the new module.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
